title: Finder rename hint omits select-all; names come out as x.txt.txt
description:
**What:** Finder's rename field selects only the base name ("draft-v1", not ".txt"), but the helper's `label_only` error and `docs/api.md` say to rename with click, `pressKey("Return")`, `typeText(name)`, `pressKey("Return")`. Following that hint turns `draft-v1.txt` into `final-report.txt.txt`. In both bench runs the agent then guessed `ctrl+a`, which on macOS moves to the start of the line, and only `super+a` fixed it.

**Evidence:** `native/macos/NostringsHelper.swift:559` and `docs/api.md:164` give the recipe without a select-all step. `bench/results/v2/transcripts.tar.gz`, finder-rename × glovebox, 2026-11-03T21-17-02 (final text: "My first attempts left the file with a doubled name") and 2026-11-03T22-22-58 (it produced "final-report.txtdraft-v1.txt"). In `bench/results/v2/summary.md` this is the one task where nostrings was not cheapest: 8.5 round trips, $0.061 and 3.5 images, against 3, $0.041 and 0 for Codex `cua_repl`.

**Why it matters:** Renaming a file in Finder is a common task. Every agent that follows the tool's own hint ends up with a wrong name, then spends round trips and screenshots fixing it.

**Done when:** The helper message, `docs/api.md` and the skill say `pressKey("cmd+a")` after `Return` (or say to type the name without its extension). Then `node bench/run.mjs --setups nostrings --tasks finder-rename --n 2` passes 2/2 with a median of 4 round trips or fewer, 0 images, and a cost under $0.041.

**Size:** small (under an hour), plus one helper rebuild and a bench run.

<!-- discovery: scout C -->
notes: Text fixed in helper label_only message, docs/api.md, SKILL.md (super+a after Return). Open until helper rebuild and bench finder-rename --n 2 run.

title: macOS background route steals focus from the user while driving Firefox
description: Report 2026-11-23 (macOS 27, Firefox 160): while an agent drove Firefox on the background route, Firefox kept taking focus from the app the user was in. Every action reported lastRoute background or accessibility, so the steal happens outside what withInputRoute checks. Suspects: app.menu('File > New Window'); app.focus on the URL bar (AXFocused); pressKey Return; pressKey super+alt+k opening an undocked DevTools window 1-3 s later (after the 60 ms check); AXPress on DevTools Console Settings; the first read setting AXEnhancedUserInterface; makeWindowKey's SLPS records reordering Firefox's windows.
design: 1. With TextEdit frontmost, run each action alone via node bin/nostrings.mjs run and log the frontmost app every 50 ms for 5 s. 2. For late activations, watch ~2 s after window-opening background actions and restore the user's app, or report it in lastRoute. 3. Smoke check: fixture opens a new window and a secondary window in the background; assert frontmost unchanged for 3 s. Also record lastRoute in actions.log.
acceptance_criteria: The new smoke check passes, and the Firefox sequence above leaves the user's app frontmost.

title: js sandbox: scripts can reach the real process and fetch
description: The kernel runs cells in a vm context, which is not a security boundary. setTimeout.constructor("return process")() returns the host process (src/kernel.mjs, context setup), and fetch is exposed to scripts. Anyone who can send a cell (the agent, or a prompt injection that reaches it) can run arbitrary code as the user, not only GUI actions. SECURITY.md now states this as a known limitation.
design: Options: run the kernel under sandbox-exec (deny network, limit file writes), drop fetch from the context, freeze/replace timer constructors. Isolation must land before any remote gateway work.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test shows setTimeout.constructor('return process')() and fetch are unavailable inside a cell, or the kernel process is sandboxed and the test shows a denied file write / network call.

title: getAXState({root}) to expand one folded outline subtree
description:
**What:** A large tree prints as an outline whose folded lines end in `(+N inside)`, but there is no way to print just one folded subtree. The only choices are `{full: true}`, which prints every element (often thousands of lines), or `find()`/`nodes()`, which return data and no tree. Add `getAXState({root: index})` to print the subtree under one element, with the same outline limit and diffing.

**Evidence:** `src/api.mjs:291-292` builds the outline and the `(+N inside)` marker, and the only escape it offers is `{full: true}` (`src/api.mjs:315`). agent-desktop documents this exact flow for dense apps: "use `--skeleton --compact` to map the app, then `--root <ref>` to drill into one region" (https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop).

**Why it matters:** Mail, Xcode, Finder lists and browsers go over 250 elements. Today an agent that needs one folded region either reads the whole tree, at a large token cost, or writes `nodes()` filtering code by hand. This fits the diffs-over-screenshots design and is not on the roadmap's token list.

**Done when:** A unit test in `test/unit.test.mjs` uses a fake backend with a tree of more than 250 elements. `getAXState({root: i})` on a folded element prints only that element and its descendants, with no line from outside the subtree, and a second identical call prints `no change`. `docs/api.md` documents `root`.

**Size:** medium (a session).

<!-- discovery: scout B -->

title: nostrings script args drop leading zeros: code=012345 becomes 12345
description:
**What:** `nostrings script <name> key=value` turns every value that looks numeric into a Number. Leading zeros are lost and blanks become 0, so a one-time code, a ZIP code or an all-digit adb serial reaches the script changed.

**Evidence:** `src/scripts.mjs:75`, `raw !== "" && !Number.isNaN(Number(raw)) ? Number(raw) : raw`. Run here: `parseArgPairs(["code=012345","zip=02134","serial=0123456789","x= "])` returns `{ code: 12345, zip: 2134, serial: 123456789, x: 0 }`. `test/unit.test.mjs:378` only checks `a=2`.

**Why it matters:** Saved scripts get rerun from a shell with no model watching. The shipped examples take `serial`, `text` and codes (`examples/phone-code-to-mac.js`, `examples/textedit-note.js`), so a changed value gets typed or used without anyone seeing it.

**Done when:** A unit test asserts `parseArgPairs(["code=012345","x= "])` deep-equals `{ code: "012345", x: " " }`, so only canonical numbers convert (`String(Number(raw)) === raw`), and `npm test` passes. `docs/cli.md` says which values convert.

**Size:** small (under an hour).

title: Skill and tool text: retry in background before {foreground:true}
description: Field report: after one DevTools step the agent passed {foreground:true} on nearly every action, so Firefox stayed frontmost and the user switching apps tripped the switched-away stop. skills/nostrings/SKILL.md still just says to pass foreground.
design: Skill and js tool description: retry the failing action once in the background with {window: <title>} before foreground. Consider a one-line notice when foreground is used while background was never tried in that window. Maintainer decision: should the stop apply when the agent forced foreground?
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md and the js tool description say to retry in the background first; a unit test covers any new notice.

title: False 'user switched away' stop on the foreground route
description: Field report 2026-11-05 (macOS 27, Firefox): a cell of {foreground:true} scrolls and screenshots stopped with 'Stopped: the user switched away from Firefox' though the user says they did not switch. Nothing recorded what was frontmost, so another app taking focus cannot be ruled out. src/api.mjs #activate(): the second action in a cell checks isActive and a single false reading ends the call. docs/recipes.md section 7 tells the agent not to continue, so a false stop halts work.
acceptance_criteria: The Stopped message or the action log names the frontmost app when the stop fires; and the cause is found, or isActive is re-read once after a short delay before stopping.

title: Firefox: about:preferences content missing from background read
description: Background read of a Firefox window on about:preferences#privacy returned 82 nodes and no web area (chrome only), even after 4 s. Web pages in the same window read fine. Firefox 160, nostrings 0.6.0 build.
acceptance_criteria: A background read of about:preferences includes the page content (e.g. the site-data search field).

title: Horizontal background scroll (dx): retest on a remote-desktop viewer
description: A field run on a remote-desktop viewer (2026-10-29) found scroll(target,{dx:15}) had no effect on a remote table while dy worked; scrollbar-arrow clicks worked. Point and fixed-point axis-2 deltas are now set (2acf938) but not retried on a remote-desktop viewer.
acceptance_criteria: scroll(target,{dx}) moves a wide table horizontally in a remote-desktop viewer in the background.

title: Android phase 4: tree quality, text and speed
description: Fixture hardening (list reuse, WebView, Compose, split one-time-code field), event-driven waitForChange, large-tree outline and silent lookups, host OCR for one-node trees. Only the bench item is left.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture suite passes; bench shows round trips and cost per task.

title: Android bench: round trips and cost per task
description: Extend bench/ to drive fixture or stock-app tasks through ui.device() and report calls, tokens and time.
acceptance_criteria: Bench report includes Android tasks with round trips and cost.

title: Android phase 3: virtual-display sessions
description: One display per session with scrcpy's per-API flags, destroyed with its content on teardown; per-action check that the task is still on the session display; keyboard policy; parallel named sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Default-display-untouched checks (focus, screenshot hash, emulator console capture) pass across the matrix with two sessions running.

title: Android backend: reach parity per docs/internal/android-plan.md
description: Android as a second backend behind the backend protocol, with an on-device shell server (app_process). Target: coding agents testing Android apps on an emulator or a dedicated test phone. Phases 1-2 shipped. Test devices: Android Studio emulators (API 34-37) and one physical Android 17 test phone; daily development uses the API 36 emulator only.

title: Bench v2 report: six-setup chart, group by model and effort, Wilson intervals
description: report.mjs mixes models if result files differ. Group by model+effort, add Wilson 95% intervals on pass rates, extend the validated palette from 3 to 6 series, and move the 10-28 baseline out of raw/. Speed chart already added.
acceptance_criteria: node bench/report.mjs on v2 results writes a summary with per-model/effort groups and intervals.

title: Bench v2: pilot N=1, then full run within the budget cap
Bench metrics: focus steals, cursor moved, p90, Wilson intervals, model and effort columns
Benchmark v2: harder tasks, more setups, Haiku axis
description: Tooling-only comparison: one Claude API loop, only the computer-use tool changes. Codex computer use runs without Codex through its stdio MCP server. Models: Sonnet 5.5 medium and Haiku 5.5 with an effort sweep; no Opus. Budget cap set by the maintainer before the full run. Open question from v1: Codex lost the first record's department field in form and bulk-entry tasks three times; cause unknown.

title: OCR diff and long-list recipe: try on a real remote-desktop session
description: Drawn screens (a remote-desktop viewer exposes one node) now steer agents to OCR, and repeat OCR reads return a diff. Only tested on local fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: On a remote-desktop viewer, two OCR reads around a scroll return a diff that names only the changed lines.

title: Saved scripts: run the Mac examples after a helper rebuild
description: ui.scripts.save/list/run/source and the examples/ gallery shipped. Phone examples were tested on the emulator; the Mac examples (calc, textedit-note, phone-code-to-mac) are untested until the helper is rebuilt.
acceptance_criteria: nostrings script <name> runs each Mac example in examples/ and it does what its header says.

title: Android listApps: report active app so 'switched away' stop names it
description: ns-e8w added the frontmost app to the 'user switched away' stop via listApps active flag. macOS reports active; Android listApps may not, so the stop says 'frontmost app unknown'. Add active (from topPackage(display)) to Device.java listApps.

title: Sanctioned telemetry sink for field runs
description: Sessions have no fs/require, so per-call telemetry in a field run had to be printed and re-parsed from the agent transcript. Consider ui.log(obj) appended to actions.log, or a scratch-file writer.
acceptance_criteria: A cell can call ui.log({..}) and the object appears as one JSON line in actions.log.

title: Firefox: background Escape does not close the DevTools console-settings menu
description: After background AXPress opened the Console Settings menu in undocked DevTools, pressKey('Escape', {window: devtools}) left the menu open 0.5 s later. Recheck now that windows are matched by AX window number (frame matching gave DevTools the same id as another window).
acceptance_criteria: pressKey('Escape', {window}) closes the menu within 0.5 s in the background.

title: Android phase 6: prove parity
description: Full Android bench including an AndroidWorld comparison; Android sections in api.md, agents.md and SECURITY.md; emulator matrix in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Every parity-map row done or documented as a limit; README Status lists Android with tested versions.

title: Android phase 5: physical phones
description: USB then wireless ADB with reconnect and re-pair; doctor probes each capability and names the vendor toggle; device matrix and physical-only checks from the plan's test strategy. Carry-overs from phase 3: check the wake lock on a physical phone with auto-sleep on, and run the virtual-display probe that was only run on emulators. Re-run the physical phone after the usability and web-typing work.
acceptance_criteria: Published support matrix per device and Android version.

title: Android: moved_to_phone_screen error is untested
description: No app has been seen moving itself from a hidden display to the phone's screen, so the check in appWindows never fired. It only fires when the hidden display is empty; an app that opens a second activity on display 0 while its main one stays hidden is not detected.
acceptance_criteria: A probe or fixture activity that launches onto display 0 produces the coded error.

title: Test nostrings with claude -p (non-interactive Claude Code)
description: README says claude -p with the MCP tool is untested. Approval prompts and the MCP server lifetime may behave differently without a TTY.
acceptance_criteria: A claude -p run that opens Calculator and computes 2+2 through the js tool exits 0 and prints 4; README updated with the result.

title: Fork surface: good-first issues and a social preview image
description: Conformance check, fake backend template, CONTRIBUTING porting guide and Discussions are done. Left: label a few good-first issues on GitHub and set the repo social preview image.
acceptance_criteria: At least three open GitHub issues carry good first issue, and the repo settings show a social preview image.

title: Remote gateway: drive the Mac from web chat clients
description: Idea (analysis only, nothing built): an MCP gateway so web chat clients (Claude, then others) can drive the Mac. Order: kernel isolation first; a vendor probe with echo tools only; Claude gateway with a bearer token; OAuth with DCR and PKCE for other clients; docs and doctor. Policy: allowlist-only remote apps, a read tool marked readOnlyHint, ~45 s call cap, full tree read at the start of a new chat. Untested: lid closed or screen locked.

title: Android phase 7: beyond parity
description: Allowlisted intents and deep links, AppFunctions if shell can call them, on-phone setup via Shizuku, work profile or dedicated phone for agent apps.
acceptance_criteria: Each item shipped or rejected with a reason in the Android plan.
